rationale: Critical RBAC regression: `if creator_id:` on line 504 is falsy for None, so legacy projects with created_by=NULL skip remove_project, _sync_project_budget_member_removed, and invalidate_user_from_cache entirely — the original inheritance bug persists for that class of projects. Both required lenses ran cleanly; 0 deferred; 3 dismissed as noise (return-value log gap, flush-rollback, test-class wording).

business_review.notes: Skipped when creator_id=None; same guard as AC2/AC3.

findings.title: Falsy guard skips cleanup for NULL creator_id
findings.problem: `if creator_id:` on line 504 evaluates to False when creator_id is None. Legacy projects whose `created_by` column is NULL reach the deletion success path with no call to remove_project, _sync_project_budget_member_removed, or invalidate_user_from_cache. The router passes `authorized_project.created_by` directly, which is nullable.
findings.impact: The original RBAC bug — Project Admin row surviving into a same-name recreated project — persists for any project with a NULL created_by. A user recreating such a project inherits stale admin membership from the deleted one.
findings.recommendation: Change `if creator_id:` to `if creator_id is not None:` on line 504. Alternatively, implement a fallback that queries and removes all UserProject rows by project_name when creator_id is absent, ensuring no membership survives for any deletion path.

findings.title: No test for creator_id=None deletion path
findings.problem: No test passes creator_id=None to delete_project and asserts that remove_project and invalidate_user_from_cache are not called and that the deletion completes without error.
findings.impact: A future change removing or altering the None guard will re-introduce the RBAC bug on legacy projects and go undetected by the test suite.
findings.recommendation: Add a test: call delete_project with creator_id=None and assert remove_project and invalidate_user_from_cache are never called while the project deletion succeeds.
